messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] plans for compatibility with Hadoop 2.0.x
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

You are right, RHIPE works with 0.20 and not Hadoop 2. Fixing RHIPE for Hadoop 2 will make it incompatible with Hadoop 1.  Currently we are rewriting RHIPE, and I guess it will be ready when CDH4 is ready (at Mozilla we use CHD3 and will move to CHD4 sometime in the near future).

This is the most recent RHIPE:

https://github.com/downloads/saptarshiguha/RHIPE/Rhipe_0.70.tar.gz

and for this you'll need to downgrade Hadoop ...

Sorry for that.

Regards
Saptarshi

messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] running rhipe on amazon emr
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jonathan,

Have you tried these insructions: http://people.mozilla.org/~sguha/ec2-installation/

I tried it recently, (Oct 02, 2012) and it worked. Always helpful if another pair of eyes tried it out too.

If you have problems following the instructions, post to the group.

Also, though in the example above you have to SSH into the node to run things, it is not required.
If you install RHIPE on your local computer and point HADOOP_HOME, HADOOP_CONF to the whirr location,
you can run RHIPE front end on your local computer and the jobs will run on the nodes.

Cheers
Saptarshi

messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] Error: could not find function "rhlm" while Linear regression
messages.subject_clean: [rhipe] Error: could not find function "rhlm" while Linear regression
messages.body_plain:
i dont recommend using rhlm anymore. Many things changed. You might want to look at the logic and rewrite the code yourself.
Essentially, it computes  (X'X)^{-1}X'Y

Get X via model.matrix and assuming the number of columns is not too large, compute X'X via map reduce. Be aware when using model.matrix the function is aware of /all/ levels of factors , not just those present in your split.

Compute X'Y

and ncol(model,matrix)) is not too large, X'X will be small.

I'm sure there are plenty of optimizations possible since the model matrix is very sparse (when factors are present).

> 1.How to create the environment variables PKG_CONFIG_PATH and LD_LIBRARY_PATH and should I create any other environment variables?

You might or not might need eitther, depending on how your installation is. However mine looks like

export PKG_CONFIG_PATH=$PKG_CONFIG_PATH:$PREFIX/lib/pkgconfig/
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$PREFIX/lib/:$PREFIX/lib64:$PREFIX/lib64//R/lib:/usr/java/jdk1.6.0_26/jre/lib/amd64/server/

PREFIX is my custom installation directory

messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] problem with print.jobtoken()
messages.body_plain:
I was using rhex() as it's used in the example at www.datadr.org <http://www.datadr.org>!

Is there a more up-to-date example? If not, perhaps you could update the airline data example there?

I noticed a few issues with the code:
1) As you point out in another post here on the Groups site, line 27 of the "Converting to R Objects" code should be "month=mn" not "month-mn"
2) Line 7 of "Using hadoop as a queryable database" should have "day" not "mday"
3) In line 19 of the same code chunk, I'm getting an error that "k" is not found in "rhcollect(k, collec". Should this be "reduce.key" rather than "k"?

Chris
